decision: Use one shared Qwen-compatible model endpoint for logical agents.
Never expose unrestricted shell or unrestricted SQL as tools.
Use deterministic verification as the success gate.
Implement inspect_vector as the only executable skill in Checkpoint 1.
Use an external Docker-managed named volume for persistent PostGIS storage and attach PostGIS declaratively to both the GeoServer default network and geoagent-backend.
Implement PostGIS validation as a deterministic read-only verifier, separate from LLM agents, using fixed SQL and validated identifiers.
Derive final workflow success exclusively from deterministic PostGIS validation and generate a secret-redacted JSON trace and Markdown report for every completed workflow.
Verify report and trace roots are writable before any database execution and block all artifact overwrites.
Build Planner Agent context deterministically from fixed trusted project files, include only implemented skills, bound context size, record source hashes, and redact secrets before model access.

Treat Planner Agent model output as untrusted JSON and require Pydantic schema validation plus deterministic skill, approval, ordering, validation, and no-execution policy checks before accepting a plan.

Run the Planner Agent in an independent non-root read-only container connected only to the model network, with read-only manifest and context mounts and no PostGIS credentials, GIS data, MCP execution access, artifact mounts, or Docker socket.

Bind every human approval to the SHA-256 digest of one canonical validated plan and an explicit set of approval-required step IDs; reject changed, expired, denied, incomplete, or overwritten approvals.

Translate only the exact approved four-step vector-to-PostGIS plan into one typed run_vector_postgis_workflow execution envelope; reject mismatched paths, targets, schemas, identifiers, arguments, approvals, skill order, or execution claims.

Use MCP Streamable HTTP only on the internal Docker control network, retain STDIO for local tests, publish no host port, restrict expected Host and Origin values, and keep write tools disabled by default.

Allow the Executor to call only one composite approval-gated MCP workflow; independently reload and verify the exact plan, approval, digest, envelope, schemas, and step scope inside the GIS container before controlled execution, and derive success only from deterministic validation.

Build the Critic context deterministically from trusted trace and report roots, enforce path and size limits, validate trace consistency, redact secrets, preserve evidence hashes, and treat incomplete evidence separately from validated success.

Run the Critic Agent as an independent non-root read-only container with model-network access only, read-only trace and report mounts, no MCP or PostGIS access, and deterministic policy that prevents the model from changing status or making unsupported success claims.

Separate GitHub-hosted CI into secret-free Python 3.12 offline tests and independent non-root container builds, while keeping Ollama, PostGIS, approval-gated execution, and other laptop-dependent integration tests outside hosted CI until a secured self-hosted runner is designed.

Represent model, MCP, execution, validation, cancellation, dependency, and internal failures using a stable secret-redacted taxonomy with deterministic exit codes and retry dispositions; permit retry only for explicitly safe read-only operations, require manual review for uncertain or interrupted database writes, and persist structured failure evidence in traces and reports.

Persist each workflow lifecycle as a schema-validated, secret-redacted state record with append-only transitions, monotonic revisions, atomic writes, exact plan and approval identity, and deterministic resume assessment; allow continuation only before execution begins, require manual review whenever a PostGIS write may have started, and expose state to the Executor through a read-only mount without implementing automatic retry or execution.

Manage versioned GeoAgent artifacts through one central schema registry, require explicit schema versions before Pydantic validation, fail closed on missing, invalid, unsupported older, and unknown future versions, write only the current registered version, and provide read-only compatibility and migration assessments without silently modifying or migrating artifacts.

Execute reusable recipes only through a typed SHA-256-bound recipe envelope, exact step-scoped human approval, and the fixed composite run_approved_recipe MCP tool; allow the independent Executor to call only health_check and the two approval-gated composite workflow tools, keep GIS libraries, data mounts, output writes, and credentials out of the Executor, independently reload and verify recipes, approvals, schemas, registry metadata, and envelopes inside the non-root GIS container, dispatch only hard-coded implemented skills, and derive recipe success from deterministic per-step validation.

Persist each completed approved recipe run inside the non-root GIS container as an immutable digest-addressed RecipeRunResult, cryptographic RecipeRunEvidence record, artifact-lineage manifest, and deterministic Markdown report; return the validated run result and durable references through a typed MCP response, independently verify the run-result digest and approved recipe identity inside the Executor, keep evidence storage and GIS output inaccessible to the Executor, prohibit overwrite and automatic replay, and require manual review whenever execution completes but durable persistence is incomplete.

Treat local-model output as an untrusted, non-executable RecipeProposal limited to fixed allowlisted templates; require schema validation, deterministic readiness assessment, trusted template compilation, recipe-policy validation, and an explicit operator save before the existing approval and execution boundaries. The model receives no shell, MCP, filesystem-write, database-write, approval, or execution authority.

Separate natural-language recipe review from persistent storage: generate and assess untrusted model proposals without writes, compile only fixed trusted templates, return clarification as a valid non-error outcome, render deterministic operator summaries, and permit immutable recipe storage only through a separate explicit command that reloads the review, verifies its schema, deterministically recompiles the proposal, and rejects any mismatch. Approval and execution remain separate later boundaries.

Generate new GIS skill skeletons only as isolated, non-overwriting, untrusted scaffold bundles; derive approval and validation requirements deterministically from skill access, keep generated registry entries planned with no executable entrypoint or verifier, validate bundles without importing generated code, and require separate human implementation, contract testing, and promotion before live registration.

Export only exact approved recipes into immutable digest-addressed Snakemake packages whose canonical Snakefile contains no shell rule and calls one trusted replay adapter; run Snakemake in a separate non-root control-network container with no model, GIS stack, PostGIS credentials, or direct output mount; independently revalidate the export, recipe, approval, digest, and step scope before invoking the existing Executor-to-MCP boundary, and write a completion marker only after deterministic validated success and durable evidence persistence.
